### Indexing and reconciliation
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/accept-indexing

> List inbound transfers, paginate, dedupe, and reconcile against your product ledger.

`GET /v1/payments/transfers` is the workhorse for reconciliation. By default, it returns paginated persisted transfer records across your organization's custody wallets, with filters for direction, status, token, exact `custodyWalletId`, and date range. Use it to mirror SDP transfers locally, match inbound payments to orders, and drive a delta-polling worker. To include recent on-chain observations for one exact wallet, set `custodyWalletId` and `includeObserved=true`.

For one feed of past payments and issuance transactions, with cursor pagination and search by ID or signature, use [Transaction history](/docs/payments/transactions). It lists persisted records only, so keep using this endpoint with `includeObserved=true` for observed on-chain activity.

## Listing inbound transfers

The minimal inbound-only request:

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers?direction=inbound&pageSize=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="list-inbound-transfers.ts"
const url = new URL("https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers");
url.searchParams.set("direction", "inbound");
url.searchParams.set("pageSize", "50");

const res = await fetch(url, {
  headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_..." },
});
const { data, meta } = await res.json();
// data: Transfer[]
// meta: { total, page, pageSize, hasMore, requestId }
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `direction` | `inbound` \| `outbound` | Common filter. Inbound = payments to wallets you control. |
| `status` | `pending` \| `processing` \| `confirmed` \| `finalized` \| `failed` | Scope to a single state. |
| `custodyWalletId` | string | Exact SDP Wallet ID (`id` from `GET /v1/wallets`). |
| `includeObserved` | boolean | Default `false`. When `true`, adds recent on-chain activity for the exact `custodyWalletId`; it cannot be used without that filter. Synthetic observed rows have `custodyWalletId: null`. |
| `token` | string | Filter by token symbol or on-chain mint (exact match against the stored transfer's `token` value). |
| `from`, `to` | ISO 8601 datetime | Time-window filter on `createdAt`. Use with offset (`2026-05-14T00:00:00Z`). |
| `page` | integer | Default `1`. |
| `pageSize` | integer | Default `20`, max `100`. |

## Deduplication

Two natural dedup keys:

1. **`Transfer.id`** — SDP-internal, immutable, present on every transfer (including `pending` ones with no signature yet). Use this as your local primary key.
2. **`Transfer.signature`** — the on-chain signature, populated once the transaction has been built and observed on-chain (typically at `confirmed`/`finalized`, but treat its presence rather than the status enum as the trigger — `processing` and even `pending` records can still have a null signature). **`UNIQUE` across SDP's transfers table** wherever it is set; two records cannot share a signature. Use this if you need to dedupe across multiple data sources (SDP + a parallel chain indexer, say) — only once `signature` is present.

In practice: store transfers in your reconciliation table keyed by SDP `Transfer.id`, and assert `signature` uniqueness once it is populated.

## Reconciling an order

Customer-initiated inbound transfers do **not** populate `Transfer.memo` (memo-program instructions aren't extracted into the field), and the inbound record doesn't expose a reference. The reliable on-record correlation key is the inbound transfer's `destination` — match it against an order whose pre-issued receiving address is that same `destination`.

The typical inbound match cycle:

1. **Read** recent persisted inbound transfers for the relevant token:
   ```text title="Request"
   GET /v1/payments/transfers
     ?direction=inbound
     &token=<mint or SOL>
     &from=<since last reconciled>
     &to=<now>
     &pageSize=100
   ```
2. **For each transfer**, look up an open order keyed by the transfer's `destination` (`findOrderByDestination(tr.destination)`).
3. **If matched**, assert the amount and token match the expected values on the order row, then mark the order paid, record the SDP `Transfer.id`, and dispatch downstream side effects (email, shipment, ledger entry).
4. **If unmatched**, leave the transfer for the next pass (it may be an early-arrival for an order you haven't staged yet) or flag it for manual review after a grace window.

If you need memo- or Solana-Pay-`reference`-based correlation (e.g., a single-wallet flow where the destination address is shared across orders), read the on-chain transaction directly via Solana RPC using the transfer's `signature`. SDP does not surface either field on inbound transfer records today.

## Solana Pay reference accounts (roadmap)

SDP does not attach a Solana Pay reference pubkey on-chain, and inbound transfer records do not expose a reference field today. The realistic correlation options are: (a) **per-order destination addresses** — pre-issue a fresh receiving wallet per order and match by `Transfer.destination` (the recommended pattern; see [Reconciling an order](#reconciling-an-order) above); (b) **on-chain reads via Solana RPC** keyed off the transfer's `signature`, used to recover the memo-program instruction or Solana Pay `reference` that SDP itself doesn't surface for inbound transfers.

## A delta-poll worker

A reconciliation worker that wakes on a tick and asks "what is new since last time":

<Tabs items={["TypeScript"]}>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="reconcile-tick.ts"
const OVERLAP_MS = 5_000; // re-query the last 5s on each tick to catch boundary arrivals

async function reconcileTick(state: WorkerState) {
  // Nudge `from` backwards by the overlap window; `alreadySeen` dedupes the
  // resulting duplicates. Always advance the high-water mark to `to` regardless,
  // otherwise the window grows without bound.
  const fromMs = state.lastSeenIso
    ? Date.parse(state.lastSeenIso) - OVERLAP_MS
    : Date.now() - 60_000;
  const from = new Date(fromMs).toISOString();
  const to = new Date().toISOString();

  // This lists persisted records. To discover additional recent chain activity,
  // run the same window per exact wallet with custodyWalletId + includeObserved.
  for await (const tr of listInbound({ from, to })) {
    if (await alreadySeen(tr.id)) continue;

    // Match by destination — the on-record correlation key for inbound transfers.
    // `tr.memo` is omitted (undefined) for customer-initiated inbound payments.
    const order = await findOrderByDestination(tr.destination);
    if (!order) {
      await persistUnmatched(tr);
      continue;
    }

    if (tr.status === "finalized") {
      await markOrderPaid(order, tr);
    }
    await persistSeen(tr.id, tr.status);
  }

  state.lastSeenIso = to;
}
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Notes:

- The overlap window (5s above) re-queries the trailing edge of the last tick to catch transfers that arrive at the boundary; `alreadySeen` collapses the resulting duplicates.
- The high-water mark advances to `to` on every pass even though `from` is rolled back — otherwise the query window grows unbounded.
- Always re-fetch a transfer to upgrade its status: a transfer seen as `confirmed` in one tick will appear as `finalized` in a later tick.
- Use `pageSize=100` and the async iterator pattern (see [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts)) to handle large windows.

## Related

- [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification) — single-transfer status reads.
- [Accept overview](/docs/payments/accept-overview) — the broader inbound flow.
- [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts) — the same list endpoint used outbound.
- [Transaction history](/docs/payments/transactions) — one cursor-paginated feed across payments and issuance.
- [Payments API reference](/docs/reference/api/payments) — full endpoint reference.

---

## Payments — Counterparties

### Counterparties
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/counterparties

> Create and manage the customer and beneficiary records that payouts and ramps use, their payment accounts, and their readiness for each ramp provider.

A **counterparty** is an identity record for a customer or beneficiary: someone you pay, bill, or move funds on- and off-ramp for. The counterparty is the *who*. Its **accounts** are the *where*: the Solana wallets that payments go to.

Several payment flows take a counterparty instead of a raw address:

- **Transfer batches and recurring payments** take a `counterpartyId` plus a `counterpartyAccountId` for each recipient, and pay that account's Solana address. See [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts).
- **Onramp quotes** (`POST /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote`) require a `counterpartyId`. The ramp provider's own customer record may be resolved or created from that counterparty. See [Ramps](/docs/payments/ramps).

The Counterparties API has 13 operations, covering field options, the counterparty records, their payment accounts, the provider accounts ramp providers hold for them, and ramp requirements.

## Permissions and project scope

| Operation | Permission |
| --- | --- |
| `GET` on any counterparty path | `counterparties:read` |
| `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` on any counterparty path | `counterparties:write` |

The `api_admin` and `api_developer` key roles include both permissions. `api_readonly` includes only `counterparties:read`. See [Authentication](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication).

Counterparties belong to a project. A counterparty created with an API key belongs to that key's project, and every counterparty call is limited to it: an ID from another project returns `404`. With an API key, the `x-project-id` header is ignored.

## Field options

`GET /v1/counterparties/metadata` returns the option sets for building a counterparty form:

- `fields.entityTypes`: the allowed `entityType` values, `individual` and `business`.
- `fields.countries`: the supported countries, each with an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 `code` and an English `name`.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties/metadata \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

## Create a counterparty

`POST /v1/counterparties` creates an active counterparty and returns `201` with the record under `data.counterparty`.

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entityType` | yes | `individual` or `business`. |
| `displayName` | yes | 1–512 characters. A searchable, human-readable name. It is indexed and not application-encrypted, so keep it minimal. |
| `externalId` | no | 1–256 characters. Your own opaque reference for the counterparty. It is indexed: do not put personal data in it. |

`externalId` must be unique across your organization's active counterparties. If another active counterparty in the project already uses the `externalId`, the request returns `409 Conflict`.

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "entityType": "individual",
    "displayName": "Jane Doe",
    "externalId": "customer_42"
  }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="create-counterparty.ts"
const response = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    entityType: "individual",
    displayName: "Jane Doe",
    externalId: "customer_42",
  }),
});
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.counterparty.id     — "cpty_…", use it in payment and ramp requests
// data.counterparty.status — "active"
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="CreateCounterparty.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "entityType": "individual",
          "displayName": "Jane Doe",
          "externalId": "customer_42"
        }"""))
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

The counterparty record contains:

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Counterparty ID, `cpty_…`. |
| `organizationId`, `projectId` | The organization and project the counterparty belongs to. |
| `externalId` | Your reference, or `null`. |
| `entityType` | `individual` or `business`. |
| `displayName` | The display name. |
| `status` | `active` or `archived`. |
| `createdBy` | The user ID recorded as the creator, or `null`. |
| `createdAt`, `updatedAt` | ISO 8601 timestamps. |

## List, get, update, and archive

| Operation | Endpoint | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List | `GET /v1/counterparties` | Newest first. `page` (1-based, default `1`) and `pageSize` (default `20`, max `100`). The response carries `counterparties`, `total`, `page`, and `pageSize`. |
| Get | `GET /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}` | Returns active counterparties only. |
| Update | `PATCH /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}` | Send at least one of `externalId`, `entityType`, `displayName`. Set `externalId` to `null` to clear it. The same `externalId` uniqueness rule and `409` apply. |
| Archive | `DELETE /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}` | Returns `204`. |

`DELETE` archives the counterparty rather than deleting it:

- Its `status` becomes `archived`, and it disappears from the default list. Pass `includeArchived=true` to `GET /v1/counterparties` to include archived records. The parameter accepts exactly `true` or `false`.
- The counterparty's provider accounts are archived with it.
- An archived counterparty no longer resolves. `GET`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` on it return `404`, as do its requirements, its provider accounts, and listing or creating its accounts.
- It no longer holds its `externalId`, so a new counterparty can use that value.
- The API has no endpoint to restore an archived counterparty.

## Payment accounts

A counterparty account is a payment destination stored under a counterparty. The only account kind is `crypto_wallet`, a Solana wallet address. A counterparty can have several accounts, and each one has its own ID. Transfer batches and recurring payments use the account's address as the destination.

Fiat bank accounts are not counterparty accounts. Ramp providers hold those, and you read them through [provider accounts](#provider-accounts).

`POST /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/accounts` creates an account and returns `201` with the record under `data.account`.

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accountKind` | yes | `crypto_wallet`. |
| `details` | yes | `network` must be `"solana"`, and `address` must be a base58 Solana wallet address. |
| `label` | no | 1–256 characters. |
| `providerAccountData` | no | A JSON object that SDP stores with the account and returns as is. |

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties/cpty_123/accounts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountKind": "crypto_wallet",
    "label": "USDC wallet",
    "details": {
      "network": "solana",
      "address": "7xKXtg2CW87d97TXJSDpbD5jBkheTqA83TZRuJosgAsU"
    }
  }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="create-counterparty-account.ts"
const counterpartyId = "cpty_123";
const response = await fetch(
  `https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties/${counterpartyId}/accounts`,
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      accountKind: "crypto_wallet",
      label: "USDC wallet",
      details: {
        network: "solana",
        address: "7xKXtg2CW87d97TXJSDpbD5jBkheTqA83TZRuJosgAsU",
      },
    }),
  }
);
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.account.id — pass it as counterpartyAccountId in transfer batches and recurring payments
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="CreateCounterpartyAccount.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties/cpty_123/accounts"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "accountKind": "crypto_wallet",
          "label": "USDC wallet",
          "details": {
            "network": "solana",
            "address": "7xKXtg2CW87d97TXJSDpbD5jBkheTqA83TZRuJosgAsU"
          }
        }"""))
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

The account record contains `id`, `organizationId`, `projectId`, `counterpartyId`, `accountKind`, `label`, `details`, `providerAccountData`, `status` (`active` or `archived`), `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`.

| Operation | Endpoint | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List | `GET /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/accounts` | Newest first. Filters: `accountKind`, `includeArchived` (default `false`), `page`, `pageSize` (max `100`). The response carries `accounts`, `total`, `page`, and `pageSize`. |
| Get | `GET /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/accounts/{counterpartyAccountId}` | Returns active accounts only. |
| Update | `PATCH /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/accounts/{counterpartyAccountId}` | Send at least one of `label`, `details`, `providerAccountData`. Set `label` to `null` to clear it. New `details` must still contain `network: "solana"` and a valid address. `accountKind` can't be changed. |
| Archive | `DELETE /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/accounts/{counterpartyAccountId}` | Returns `204`. The account disappears from the default list, and `GET` or `PATCH` on it returns `404`. |

## Provider accounts

`GET /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/provider-accounts` lists the records that ramp providers hold for the counterparty. Each row has one of three `kind` values:

| `kind` | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `customer_link` | The link between the counterparty and the provider's own customer record. |
| `payout_account` | A fiat payout account held by the provider, for one corridor: a `fiatCurrency` and a `destinationCountry`. |
| `funding_wallet` | A wallet the provider holds for the counterparty. |

Each row carries `id`, `provider`, `kind`, `fiatCurrency`, `destinationCountry`, `paymentRail`, `status` (`active` or `archived`), `providerStatus`, and `createdAt`. `fiatCurrency` and `destinationCountry` are `null` on customer-link rows. Depending on the kind, a row can also include:

- **Payout accounts:** `bankName`, `accountNumberLast4`, and `paymentRails`. SDP fetches these from the provider when you call the endpoint, and `providerStatus` then reflects the provider's current status. Account numbers come back only as their last four digits. If the provider can't be reached, the request returns `503`.
- **Funding wallets:** `providerAccountReference`, the provider's wallet ID, and `balance`, a live balance read from the provider. `balance.state` is `available` (with `amount` as a decimal string and `currency`) or `unavailable` when the provider read fails. Both fields appear only after the provider has assigned a wallet.
- **Every row:** `customerLink`, the provider's customer link, once onboarding with that provider has started. It carries `providerCustomerReference`, `status`, and `providerStatus`. For BVNK it also carries `residenceCountryCode` and the `agreements` with their `signedAt` times.

When a provider has a customer link but no payout accounts or funding wallets, the customer link is returned as its own row.

Optional filters: `provider`, `fiatCurrency`, and `destinationCountry`. Customer-link rows always pass the currency and country filters. Rows of both statuses are returned, oldest first.

A counterparty can have more than one payout account in the same corridor. Each row records its own `paymentRail`, such as `ACH`.

## Ramp requirements

Before you request a ramp quote, check whether the counterparty is ready for the provider. `GET /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/requirements` evaluates the counterparty against one provider, direction, and asset pair. It returns the current state and any fields or provider-hosted actions the provider still needs.

| Query param | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | yes | Onramp: `moonpay`, `lightspark`, `bvnk`, `coinbase`, `stripe`. Offramp: `lightspark`, `moonpay`, `bvnk`. |
| `direction` | yes | `onramp` or `offramp`. |
| `assetRail` | yes | Canonical SDP crypto asset rail, such as `usdc.solana`. |
| `fiatCurrency` | yes | ISO currency code, such as `USD`. |
| `destinationCustodyWalletId` | onramp only | The custody wallet `id` (`cwlt_…`, from `GET /v1/wallets`) that receives the crypto. Required for onramp. Your API key must be allowed to use the wallet. |
| `destinationCountry` | no | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 payout country. Valid only for Lightspark offramp. See [Lightspark offramp corridors](#lightspark-offramp-corridors). |

A parameter that doesn't apply to the provider and direction returns `400`, for example `destinationCountry` with any provider other than Lightspark offramp. A provider that isn't offered in the current environment returns `403`.

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties/cpty_123/requirements?provider=moonpay&direction=onramp&assetRail=sol.solana&fiatCurrency=USD&destinationCustodyWalletId=cwlt_123" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="read-requirements.ts"
const url = new URL(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties/cpty_123/requirements"
);
url.searchParams.set("provider", "moonpay");
url.searchParams.set("direction", "onramp");
url.searchParams.set("assetRail", "sol.solana");
url.searchParams.set("fiatCurrency", "USD");
url.searchParams.set("destinationCustodyWalletId", "cwlt_123");

const response = await fetch(url, {
  headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_..." },
});
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.status — "ready" means you can request a quote with this provider
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="ReadRequirements.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create(
        "https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties/cpty_123/requirements"
            + "?provider=moonpay&direction=onramp&assetRail=sol.solana"
            + "&fiatCurrency=USD&destinationCustodyWalletId=cwlt_123"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .GET()
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

A counterparty that is ready for the provider returns:

```json title="Response"
{
  "data": {
    "direction": "onramp",
    "provider": "moonpay",
    "status": "ready"
  }
}
```

### Reading the response

Every response carries `provider`, `direction`, and `status`. The other fields depend on `status`:

| `status` | Providers | Extra fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | all | Lightspark offramp: `providerAccountId`, `payout` | The counterparty is ready for a quote with this provider. |
| `collect` | all | `fields` | The provider needs the data described in `fields`. |
| `collect_counterparty` | `lightspark`, `bvnk` | `fields` | The provider needs details about the counterparty, described in `fields`. |
| `collect_counterparty_residence` | `bvnk` | `fields` | The provider needs the counterparty's tax-residence country before anything else. |
| `collect_account` | `lightspark` | `payout` | Lightspark offramp needs a payout account for the corridor. See [Lightspark offramp corridors](#lightspark-offramp-corridors). |
| `counterparty_collect_agreement` | `bvnk` | `agreements` | The counterparty must accept the listed provider agreements. Each has `name`, `displayName`, `description`, `url`, and `privacyPolicyUrl`. |
| `counterparty_agreement_signing` | `bvnk` | none | Agreement acceptance is being confirmed with the provider. |
| `onboarding_not_started` | `lightspark` | none | Onboarding with the provider hasn't started. |
| `customer_verification_required` | `bvnk` | `verificationUrl` | The provider needs the counterparty to complete verification on a provider-hosted page. BVNK generates a new link for each response. |
| `customer_verifying` | `bvnk` | none | The provider is reviewing the counterparty. |
| `customer_verification_failed` | `bvnk` | none | Verification failed at the provider. |
| `customer_funding_account_provisioning` | `bvnk` | none | The provider is setting up a funding account for the counterparty. |
| `customer_funding_account_provisioning_failed` | `bvnk` | none | Funding-account setup failed at the provider. |
| `unsupported` | all | `reason` | The provider doesn't support this request for the counterparty, for example because of the fiat currency. `reason` explains why. |

The in-progress states `counterparty_agreement_signing`, `customer_verifying`, and `customer_funding_account_provisioning` change on the provider's side. Read the requirements again to see the current state.

Each entry in `fields` describes one value the provider needs:

| Property | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | `text`, `select`, `country`, `currency`, `date`, or `address`. |
| `key` | Field identifier. Nested values use dotted keys, such as `customer.address.line1`. |
| `label` | Human-readable label. |
| `required` | Whether the provider requires the value. |
| `pattern`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `placeholder`, `mask` | Optional constraints on `text` fields. |
| `options` | `select`: the allowed `value`/`label` pairs. `country` and `currency`: an optional subset of codes; when absent, every supported code is allowed. |
| `before` | `date`: an ISO date the value must fall before. |
| `fields` | `address`: the nested parts of the address, each described the same way. |

### Lightspark offramp corridors

For Lightspark offramp, a corridor is the requested `fiatCurrency` plus a destination country. The `payout` object describes it:

- `countryRails` maps each supported destination country to the payment rails available there, as `value`/`label` pairs.
- `railFields` maps each rail to the bank-account fields it needs, in the same format as `fields`.
- `accounts` lists the counterparty's active Lightspark payout accounts for the currency. Each has `id`, `destinationCountry`, `paymentRail`, the provider-reported `status`, and, when the provider returns them, `bankName` and `accountNumberLast4`.

Because a counterparty can hold several payout accounts, `destinationCountry` controls the result once the earlier Lightspark requirements are met:

- Without `destinationCountry`, the status is `collect_account`, and existing accounts appear in `payout.accounts`.
- With `destinationCountry`, if exactly one account in `accounts` for that country has the provider status `ACTIVE`, the status is `ready` and `providerAccountId` is that account's `id`.
- With `destinationCountry`, if more than one such account matches, the request returns `400`.
- With `destinationCountry`, if none matches, the status is `collect_account`.

An abbreviated `collect_account` response for `usdc.solana` to `USD`, trimmed to the US rails and the two required ACH fields. The full response lists every supported country in `countryRails` and every rail's fields in `railFields`:

```json title="Response"
{
  "data": {
    "direction": "offramp",
    "provider": "lightspark",
    "status": "collect_account",
    "payout": {
      "countryRails": {
        "US": [
          { "value": "ACH", "label": "ACH" },
          { "value": "FEDNOW", "label": "FedNow" },
          { "value": "RTP", "label": "RTP" },
          { "value": "WIRE", "label": "Wire" },
          { "value": "SWIFT", "label": "SWIFT" }
        ]
      },
      "railFields": {
        "ACH": [
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "key": "bankAccount.accountNumber",
            "label": "Account number",
            "required": true,
            "minLength": 1,
            "maxLength": 34,
            "placeholder": "12345678"
          },
          {
            "kind": "text",
            "key": "bankAccount.routingNumber",
            "label": "Routing number",
            "required": true,
            "pattern": "^[0-9]{9}$",
            "minLength": 9,
            "maxLength": 9,
            "placeholder": "021000021"
          }
        ]
      },
      "accounts": []
    }
  }
}
```

## Data handling

- **The counterparty record holds no identity data.** It has no fields for email, address, date of birth, or tax ID. It stores `displayName`, `entityType`, and your optional `externalId`, plus IDs, status, and timestamps.
- **`displayName` and `externalId` are indexed and not application-encrypted.** Keep `displayName` minimal, and don't put personal data in `externalId`.
- **Provider-collected data isn't stored.** Identity and bank details that a provider needs, as described by `fields` or `payout` in the requirements response, belong to the provider; SDP doesn't persist them. SDP keeps only the provider-side references and onboarding state it needs for later requests, such as provider customer IDs, statuses, BVNK's tax-residence country and agreement signing times, and Lightspark's purpose-of-payment code.
- **Bank details are read from the provider on request.** Provider accounts and Lightspark offramp requirements fetch payout-account details from the provider when you call them. Responses carry the bank name and the last four digits of the account number, never the full number.

## Errors

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | Invalid body or query, or a `PATCH` with no fields. On requirements: a parameter that doesn't apply, a missing `destinationCustodyWalletId` on onramp, or more than one matching Lightspark payout account for `destinationCountry`. |
| `403` | The key lacks the required permission, the requirements provider isn't offered in this environment, or the key can't use `destinationCustodyWalletId`. |
| `404` | The counterparty or account doesn't exist, is archived, or belongs to another project. |
| `409` | Another active counterparty in the project already uses the `externalId`. |
| `503` | Provider accounts: the provider couldn't be reached for payout-account details. |

For exact request and response schemas, use the [OpenAPI JSON](https://api.solana.com/openapi.json), where these operations carry the `Counterparties` tag. The [API reference](/docs/reference/api) pages cover the other API families.

## Related

- [Ramps](/docs/payments/ramps): onramp quotes that take a `counterpartyId`.
- [Ramp providers](/docs/payments/ramps-providers): per-provider capabilities.
- [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts): transfer batches that pay counterparty accounts.
- [Authentication](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication): key roles and permissions.

---

## Payments — Ramps

### Ramps
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/ramps

> Fiat on-ramps through SDP — discover supported currencies, read counterparty requirements, create an on-ramp quote, and hand the user to the provider to pay.

SDP ramps are quote-only. You create an **on-ramp quote** (fiat to crypto) against a provider you name, and the response tells you how the end user pays that provider: a provider-hosted page, funding instructions, or an embedded widget. There is no execute endpoint. The provider completes the purchase and delivers the crypto to your custody wallet, and SDP records the ramp as a transfer you can track.

For off-ramps (crypto to fiat), the public API offers currency discovery only.

For per-provider configuration and capabilities, see [Ramp providers](/docs/payments/ramps-providers).

| Step | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Discover on-ramp currencies | `GET /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/currency` |
| Discover off-ramp currencies | `GET /v1/payments/ramps/offramp/currency` |
| Read counterparty requirements | `GET /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/requirements` |
| Create an on-ramp quote | `POST /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote` |
| Track the ramp | `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` |
| Simulate a pay-in (sandbox only) | `POST /v1/payments/ramps/sandbox/simulate` |

## Prerequisites

1. **A Counterparty** for the customer buying the crypto. Create one with `POST /v1/counterparties`.
2. **A custody wallet you control** to receive the crypto. You pass its `id` (the `id` returned by `GET /v1/wallets`).
3. **An API key** with the permissions listed under [Permissions](#permissions), whose wallet scope includes that custody wallet.
4. **The provider enabled for your organization.** See [Provider gating](/docs/payments/ramps-providers#provider-gating).

## Discovering currencies

`GET /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/currency` lists the fiat-to-crypto pairs SDP supports and which providers cover each one. `GET /v1/payments/ramps/offramp/currency` does the same for crypto-to-fiat pairs.

<Tabs items={["curl"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/currency?source=USD&dest=usdc.solana" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

All query parameters are optional filters:

| Query param | On-ramp | Off-ramp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | Fiat currency (ISO 4217 code, such as `USD`). | Crypto asset rail (`usdc.solana`, `sol.solana`, …). |
| `dest` | Crypto asset rail. | Fiat currency. |
| `provider` | Limit the results to one provider. | Limit the results to one provider. |

The response contains:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `currencies.sources`, `currencies.destinations` | Every source and destination that has at least one matching pair. |
| `pairs` | One entry per `source`/`dest` combination, with the `providers` that support it. |
| `providerDetails` | Keyed by provider, for each provider that appears in `pairs`: `currencies` (per fiat currency, `min` and `max` amounts, `null` when the provider reports no limit), `countrySupport`, and the counterparty `entityTypes` the provider accepts in this direction. |
| `supportHash` | A hash of the support data the response was built from. |

```json title="response.json"
{
  "data": {
    "currencies": {
      "sources": ["USD"],
      "destinations": ["usdc.solana"]
    },
    "pairs": [
      {
        "source": "USD",
        "dest": "usdc.solana",
        "providers": ["lightspark", "bvnk", "coinbase", "stripe"]
      }
    ],
    "providerDetails": {
      "bvnk": {
        "currencies": {
          "EUR": { "min": null, "max": null },
          "USD": { "min": null, "max": null }
        },
        "countrySupport": { "coverage": "unreported" },
        "entityTypes": ["individual"]
      }
    },
    "supportHash": "4327e937..."
  },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "timestamp": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

The example shows one `providerDetails` entry; a real response has one for every provider listed in `pairs`.

A few things to know about discovery:

- SDP answers from its own support data. It does not call the providers for this request.
- Discovery does not check which providers are enabled for your organization. A provider listed here can still return `403` when you quote, if it is not enabled for you.
- Quote requests are checked against the same on-ramp data: a provider that does not list your `assetRail` and `fiatCurrency` pair is rejected with `UNSUPPORTED_CORRIDOR`.

## Reading counterparty requirements

Some providers need information about the counterparty, or need the counterparty to complete onboarding with them, before they will quote. Read the counterparty's requirements for the provider before you quote:

<Tabs items={["curl"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/counterparties/cpty_.../requirements?provider=bvnk&direction=onramp&assetRail=usdc.solana&fiatCurrency=USD&destinationCustodyWalletId=cwlt_..." \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

| Query param | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | yes | The provider you plan to quote with. |
| `direction` | yes | `onramp`. |
| `assetRail` | yes | The crypto asset rail you plan to buy. |
| `fiatCurrency` | yes | The fiat currency the customer pays with. |
| `destinationCustodyWalletId` | yes, for `onramp` | The custody wallet that will receive the crypto. |

When the counterparty meets the provider's requirements, `status` is `ready`:

```json title="response.json"
{
  "data": {
    "provider": "bvnk",
    "direction": "onramp",
    "status": "ready"
  },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "timestamp": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

Any other `status` means the counterparty is not ready for that provider:

- `unsupported` — the provider cannot serve this request. `reason` explains why (for example, BVNK returns `"BVNK supports USD only."` for other fiat currencies).
- Any other value — the provider still needs something before it will quote. The response describes what is outstanding, for example a `fields` list or a `verificationUrl`.

MoonPay, Coinbase, and Stripe report `ready` for every on-ramp counterparty. Lightspark and BVNK report the counterparty's current state with that provider. Quoting Lightspark or BVNK before the counterparty is provisioned with them returns `409 CONFLICT`.

## Creating an on-ramp quote

`POST /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote` creates a quote with the provider you name and records a transfer for it.

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "bvnk",
    "counterpartyId": "cpty_...",
    "destinationCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_...",
    "assetRail": "usdc.solana",
    "fiatCurrency": "USD",
    "fiatAmount": "100.00"
  }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="onramp-quote.ts"
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      provider: "bvnk",
      counterpartyId: "cpty_...",
      destinationCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_...",
      assetRail: "usdc.solana",
      fiatCurrency: "USD",
      fiatAmount: "100.00",
    }),
  }
);
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.quote.deliveryMode tells you how the user pays; data.transferId tracks the ramp
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="OnrampQuote.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "provider": "bvnk",
          "counterpartyId": "cpty_...",
          "destinationCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_...",
          "assetRail": "usdc.solana",
          "fiatCurrency": "USD",
          "fiatAmount": "100.00"
        }"""))
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Request fields

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | yes | One of `moonpay`, `lightspark`, `bvnk`, `coinbase`, `stripe`. SDP does not choose a provider for you. |
| `counterpartyId` | yes | An existing Counterparty. Provider-side customer records are resolved from it on the server; you never pass provider customer IDs. |
| `destinationCustodyWalletId` | yes | The `id` of a custody wallet you control (from `GET /v1/wallets`). The crypto is delivered to this wallet's address. |
| `assetRail` | yes | The crypto asset rail to buy: `sol.solana`, `usdc.solana`, `usdt.solana`, `usdg.solana`, or `pyusd.solana`. |
| `fiatCurrency` | yes | ISO 4217 code of the currency the customer pays with. |
| `fiatAmount` | yes | Decimal string greater than zero, in fiat units (`"100.00"`). |
| `rampsMemo` | no | Up to 20 key/value string pairs (keys up to 64 characters, values up to 256), stored on the transfer as `rampsMemo` for your own reconciliation. |

Unknown fields are rejected with `400`.

Before SDP contacts the provider, it checks that your key's allowed operations include the quote (see [Allowed operations](#allowed-operations)), that the provider is offered in your key's environment and enabled for your organization, that the provider supports the `assetRail` and `fiatCurrency` pair, and that the counterparty and wallet exist and the wallet is in your key's scope.

### What the quote contains

```json title="response.json"
{
  "data": {
    "quote": {
      "id": "...",
      "provider": "bvnk",
      "status": "pending",
      "deliveryMode": "manual_instructions",
      "paymentInstructions": [
        {
          "provider": "bvnk",
          "kind": "fiat_funding",
          "onboardingStatus": "ready",
          "fundingWalletId": "...",
          "fiatCurrency": "USD",
          "beneficiaryAddress": "7xKXz...9fGh",
          "network": "SOLANA",
          "bankAccount": {
            "accountNumber": "...",
            "routingNumber": "...",
            "bankName": "...",
            "paymentReference": "SDP-ONRAMP xfr_..."
          },
          "paymentReference": "SDP-ONRAMP xfr_...",
          "instructionsNotes": "Include SDP-ONRAMP xfr_... in the bank transfer reference to receive crypto on SOLANA."
        }
      ]
    },
    "transferId": "xfr_..."
  },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "timestamp": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `transferId` | The transfer SDP created for this quote. Use it to track the ramp. |
| `quote.id` | The quote identifier. |
| `quote.provider` | The provider that created the quote. |
| `quote.status` | `pending`, `processing`, `completed`, or `failed`: the provider's state when the quote was created. SDP does not update this value afterwards, and there is no endpoint to read a quote again. Track the transfer instead. |
| `quote.deliveryMode` | How the user completes the purchase. See the next section. |
| `quote.expiresAt` | When the quote expires, if the provider reports it. |

Lightspark quotes also return the quoted economics: `exchangeRate`, `totalSendingAmount` with `sendingCurrency`, `totalReceivingAmount` with `receivingCurrency`, and `feesIncluded` with `feeCurrency`. The amounts are in the currency's smallest unit; each currency object carries its `code` and `decimals`.

### How the user completes the purchase

`quote.deliveryMode` tells you what to do next:

| `deliveryMode` | What to do | Providers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hosted` | Send the user to `quote.hostedUrl`, a page run by the provider, to pay there. | MoonPay, Coinbase |
| `manual_instructions` | Show the user `quote.paymentInstructions`: the account to send the fiat to and any reference the payment must carry. For BVNK, the bank transfer must include `paymentReference`, or the payment cannot be matched to this transfer. | Lightspark, BVNK |
| `session_widget` | Embed the provider's widget in your app. Stripe returns `quote.clientSecret`, `quote.publishableKey`, and `quote.sessionId` for its on-ramp session. | Stripe |

There is no further SDP endpoint to call. The provider moves the money and delivers the crypto to the destination wallet. As the provider reports progress, SDP updates the transfer:

- Poll `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` for one ramp, or list ramps with `GET /v1/payments/transfers?category=ramp`.
- A transfer for a `manual_instructions` quote starts at `awaiting_payment`; other quotes start at the quote's status, usually `pending`. See [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification#status-lifecycle) for every ramp transfer status.

## Allowed operations

An on-ramp quote is operation type `ramp_onramp_quote`, in the `ramp` family. If your key carries [allowed operations](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys#allowed-operations) and the list includes neither, the request returns `403` with code `OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED` before SDP validates the body or counts the request against the quote rate limit. SDP creates no quote and no transfer.

## Sandbox: simulating a pay-in

In sandbox you can have the provider simulate the customer's fiat payment, so you can test the rest of the flow without moving real money. Send the `transferId` from the quote response:

<Tabs items={["curl"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/sandbox/simulate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "transferId": "xfr_..."
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

`transferId` is the only field the request accepts. SDP reads the provider, the quote reference, the counterparty, and the fiat amount from the transfer.

A `204` response means SDP sent the simulated pay-in to the provider's sandbox. It does not mean the ramp has settled: keep polling `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` to see the status change as the provider reports progress.

Rules:

- **Sandbox only.** A request from a production key returns `403`.
- **On-ramp transfers awaiting payment.** The transfer must be an on-ramp transfer (`400` otherwise) in status `awaiting_payment` (`409` otherwise).
- **Lightspark and BVNK only.** These are the providers whose quotes wait for a pay-in (`manual_instructions`).
- **Once per transfer.** A second request for the same transfer returns `409`. If the provider call fails in a way that may have reached the provider, the attempt still counts. To try again, create a new quote and simulate its transfer.

## Permissions

| Endpoint | API key needs |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/currency`, `GET /v1/payments/ramps/offramp/currency` | `payments:read` |
| `GET /v1/counterparties/{counterpartyId}/requirements` | `counterparties:read`. For `onramp`, the key's wallet scope must include `destinationCustodyWalletId`. |
| `POST /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote` | `payments:write` and `wallets:read`. The key's `payments:write` wallet scope must include the destination wallet. |
| `POST /v1/payments/ramps/sandbox/simulate` | `payments:write`. The key's `payments:write` wallet scope must include the transfer's destination wallet. |
| `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` | `payments:read` |

See [Manage API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys) for permissions and wallet scopes.

## Errors

Errors use the standard envelope: `error.code`, `error.message`, and optional `error.details`.

| Status | Code | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `BAD_REQUEST` | The body or query fails validation, including unknown fields. Also returned for a BVNK on-ramp quote in a fiat currency other than `USD`. |
| `400` | `UNSUPPORTED_CORRIDOR` | The provider does not support the `assetRail` and `fiatCurrency` pair. `error.details.supportedProviders` lists the providers that do. |
| `403` | `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` | The API key lacks a permission listed under [Permissions](#permissions). |
| `403` | `OPERATION_NOT_ALLOWED` | The key's allowed operations include neither `ramp` nor `ramp_onramp_quote`. See [Allowed operations](#allowed-operations). |
| `403` | `FORBIDDEN` | The provider is not offered in your key's environment or not enabled for your organization, the wallet is outside your key's scope, or a sandbox simulation was requested with a production key. |
| `404` | `NOT_FOUND` | The counterparty, wallet, or transfer does not exist in your project. |
| `409` | `CONFLICT` | The counterparty is not provisioned with the provider (read its [requirements](#reading-counterparty-requirements)), or one of the sandbox simulation conflicts described above. |
| `429` | `RATE_LIMITED` | Quote rate limit reached (see below). |
| `503` | `PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | The provider has no credentials for this environment, or the provider call failed. |

For MoonPay and BVNK, SDP records the transfer before it creates the quote. If creating the quote then fails, the transfer stays, with status `failed`.

### Rate limits

Quote requests carry quotas, counted over a one-minute window:

| Endpoint | Per API key | Per organization |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote` | 20 / minute | 60 / minute |

Over either limit, the request returns `429`. The quotas fail closed: if SDP cannot read its quota counters, quote requests return `503` rather than going through unmetered.

- [Ramp providers](/docs/payments/ramps-providers) — per-provider configuration and capability matrix.
- [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification) — ramp transfer statuses.
- [Manage API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys#allowed-operations) — limit a key's operations, including `ramp_onramp_quote`.
- [Provider onboarding](/docs/reference/provider-onboarding) — how providers are activated for an organization.

---

### Ramp providers
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/ramps-providers

> Capability matrix, configuration, and per-provider notes for MoonPay, Lightspark, BVNK, Coinbase, and Stripe.

SDP currently integrates five ramp providers. They are configured at the organization level via environment variables on the SDP API deployment; the `provider` field on `POST /v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote` selects between them.

## Sandbox vs production selection

The sandbox/production mode is chosen **per request**, not at deployment time:

- The calling API key's environment picks the mode: sandbox keys (`sk_test_`) use sandbox credentials, production keys (`sk_live_`) use production credentials.
- API keys inherit their environment from their project, and dashboard requests follow the selected project's environment.

Configure both credential pairs for any provider you want to expose to test and live traffic on the same deployment — MoonPay, Lightspark, and BVNK read separate sandbox and production credentials this way. Coinbase and Stripe use a single credential pair regardless of the resolved mode (see their sections below).

## Capability matrix

The public API creates on-ramp quotes only. For off-ramps it offers currency discovery only; the off-ramp column shows which providers `GET /v1/payments/ramps/offramp/currency` lists.

| Provider | On-ramp quote | Off-ramp currency discovery | Sandbox pay-in simulation | Delivery mode | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MoonPay | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | `hosted` | On-ramp pairs cover `sol.solana` and `pyusd.solana`. Separate sandbox and production credentials. |
| Lightspark | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | `manual_instructions` | Grid API. Separate sandbox and production credentials. |
| BVNK | ✓ (USD only) | ✓ | ✓ | `manual_instructions` | Hawk auth. Separate sandbox and production credentials. |
| Coinbase | ✓ (sandbox only) | ✗ | ✗ | `hosted` | Quote creation currently fails; see [Coinbase](#coinbase). |
| Stripe | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | `session_widget` | `usdc.solana` and `sol.solana` only. No separate sandbox credentials — supply a Stripe test-mode secret key. |

## MoonPay

| Variable | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MOONPAY_API_KEY` | conditional | Production API key. Required when the request resolves to production. |
| `MOONPAY_SECRET_KEY` | conditional | Production secret used to sign onramp / offramp URLs. Paired with `MOONPAY_API_KEY`. |
| `MOONPAY_SANDBOX_API_KEY` | conditional | Sandbox API key. Required when the request resolves to sandbox. |
| `MOONPAY_SANDBOX_SECRET_KEY` | conditional | Sandbox secret. Paired with `MOONPAY_SANDBOX_API_KEY`. |
| `MOONPAY_ONRAMP_URL` | no | Override the onramp host. Defaults to MoonPay's standard URLs; the sandbox/production choice follows the [per-request rule](#sandbox-vs-production-selection). |
| `MOONPAY_OFFRAMP_URL` | no | Same idea for offramp. |

You always send canonical asset rails; SDP maps them to MoonPay's currency codes. MoonPay's on-ramp pairs cover `sol.solana` and `pyusd.solana`, so a MoonPay quote for `usdc.solana` is rejected with `UNSUPPORTED_CORRIDOR`. Check [currency discovery](/docs/payments/ramps#discovering-currencies) for the current pairs. MoonPay also rejects on-ramp quotes with a `fiatAmount` below 20.

## Lightspark

| Variable | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LIGHTSPARK_GRID_CLIENT_ID` | conditional | Production Grid API client identifier. Required when the request resolves to production. |
| `LIGHTSPARK_GRID_CLIENT_SECRET` | conditional | Production Grid API client secret. |
| `LIGHTSPARK_GRID_SANDBOX_CLIENT_ID` | conditional | Sandbox Grid API client identifier. Required when the request resolves to sandbox. |
| `LIGHTSPARK_GRID_SANDBOX_CLIENT_SECRET` | conditional | Sandbox Grid API client secret. |

Lightspark is integrated against the Grid API (`https://api.lightspark.com/grid/2025-10-13`); the sandbox/production choice follows the [per-request rule](#sandbox-vs-production-selection). `destinationCustodyWalletId` is your own custody wallet, same as every other provider. The counterparty's Lightspark customer is resolved on the server from the counterparty, not passed on the quote request; quoting before the counterparty is provisioned with Lightspark returns `409`. Lightspark's on-ramp pairs cover `USD` to `usdc.solana`.

Lightspark quotes always return `deliveryMode: "manual_instructions"` — the response carries funding instructions to display to the payer, not a redirect URL.

## BVNK

| Variable | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BVNK_WALLET_ID` | conditional | Production BVNK-side wallet used for settlement. |
| `BVNK_HAWK_AUTH_ID` | conditional | Production Hawk auth id. Paired with `BVNK_HAWK_SECRET_KEY`. |
| `BVNK_HAWK_SECRET_KEY` | conditional | Production Hawk secret key. |
| `BVNK_SANDBOX_WALLET_ID` | conditional | Sandbox BVNK wallet. Required when the request resolves to sandbox. |
| `BVNK_SANDBOX_HAWK_AUTH_ID` | conditional | Sandbox Hawk auth id. |
| `BVNK_SANDBOX_HAWK_SECRET_KEY` | conditional | Sandbox Hawk secret key. |

BVNK uses Hawk authentication. Bearer-token auth is not currently supported.

BVNK is a travel-rule / compliance-sharing provider: party details come from the counterparty's BVNK customer record, not from the quote request. An on-ramp quote needs a verified BVNK customer with a provisioned funding wallet; otherwise it returns `409`. BVNK on-ramp quotes accept `USD` only.

BVNK quotes always return `deliveryMode: "manual_instructions"` — the response carries funding-account details to display to the payer, including a `paymentReference` the bank transfer must carry.

## Coinbase

| Variable | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COINBASE_CDP_API_KEY_ID` | conditional | CDP Secret API Key id. Same key is used for sandbox and production — sandbox is flagged per-request, not by a separate credential. |
| `COINBASE_CDP_API_KEY_SECRET` | conditional | CDP Secret API Key secret. Paired with `COINBASE_CDP_API_KEY_ID`; used to sign a per-request JWT. |

Coinbase is on-ramp only. On-ramp quotes return `deliveryMode: "hosted"`: SDP creates a guest-checkout Apple Pay order and returns its payment link as `hostedUrl`.

Order creation (the quote step) is sandbox-only. Coinbase requires buyer-agreement and phone-verification timestamps that SDP does not collect, so a production request returns `503` instead of sending a false attestation. Coinbase also requires the buyer's email and phone number, which SDP does not pass on the quote, so Coinbase quote creation currently returns `400` in sandbox as well.

## Stripe

| Variable | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | conditional | Secret key, sent as the username on HTTP Basic auth. A single key serves both modes — use a `sk_test_…` key to sandbox it, `sk_live_…` for production. |
| `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | conditional | Publishable key, echoed back on the quote for the client to mount the onramp session. |

Stripe is on-ramp only, limited to `usdc.solana` and `sol.solana` as destination assets. Quotes always return `deliveryMode: "session_widget"`: a `clientSecret`, `publishableKey`, and `sessionId` to mount Stripe's crypto onramp session, plus an optional `redirectUrl`.

## Provider gating

Even when all five providers' env vars are populated, an org can be restricted to a subset. This is [**Provider Availability**](/docs/reference/provider-onboarding): a provider must be configured for the deployment and either generally available or manually activated for the organization. SDP checks this when you create a quote or simulate a sandbox pay-in — if the org lacks availability for the requested provider, the call returns `403`. Currency discovery does not apply this check. To activate or change provider availability for a deployment, see [Provider onboarding](/docs/reference/provider-onboarding).

## Choosing a provider

| Need | Lean towards |
| --- | --- |
| Fastest sandbox iteration | MoonPay or BVNK. |
| Travel-rule / compliance party metadata | BVNK. |
| Lightning-aware fiat settlement | Lightspark. |
| Broadest payment-method coverage | MoonPay (corridor-dependent). |
| Widget/session-embedded onramp UI | Stripe. |

For self-hosted deployments where only a subset of providers will ever be configured, see [Providers optional for self-hosted SDP](/docs/reference/provider-onboarding) — SDP supports running with any single provider active.

## Related

- [Ramps](/docs/payments/ramps) — currency discovery and the on-ramp quote flow.
- [Provider onboarding](/docs/reference/provider-onboarding) — activation flow.

---

## Payments — Activity

### Transaction history
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments/transactions

> List a project's payments and issuance transactions in one feed, with filters, cursor pagination, and prefix search.

`GET /v1/transactions` returns one list of your project's transactions across SDP modules, newest first. Every row has the same fields, including a `module`, a `kind`, a normalized `status`, and the module's own `moduleStatus`. Use it for an activity feed, to find a transaction from an ID or signature, or as the input to a reconciliation job. For the full record behind a row, call that module's own endpoint with the row's `moduleId`.

## What the list contains

| `module` | One row per | Full record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `payments` | Payment transfer record: the persisted records that `GET /v1/payments/transfers` returns by default | `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` |
| `issuance` | Token transaction (deploy, mint, burn, freeze, and the other token operations) | `GET /v1/issuance/transactions`, or `GET /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/transactions` for one token |

Keep these points in mind:

- **Persisted records only.** On-chain activity that `GET /v1/payments/transfers` adds with `includeObserved=true` is not in this list. If you rely on observed inbound payments, keep reading them from the transfers endpoint (see [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing)).
- **Batches appear per transaction.** SDP splits a transfer batch into Solana transactions, and each one is a `batch_pay` row. There is no row per recipient and no single row for the whole batch. Use `GET /v1/payments/transfer-batches/{batchId}` for recipient outcomes.
- **`moduleId` points at the record.** For payments it is the transfer ID (`xfr_…`). For issuance it is the token transaction ID (`ttx_…`).

The schema also lists `module` values for features that are not generally available. A module the deployment doesn't run contributes no rows, and filtering on it returns `403`; otherwise a filter goes through the same [permission check](#permissions). If you list without a `module` filter, skip rows whose `module` you don't handle.

## List transactions

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/transactions?module=payments&status=succeeded&limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="list-transactions.ts"
const url = new URL("https://api.solana.com/v1/transactions");
url.searchParams.set("module", "payments");
url.searchParams.set("status", "succeeded");
url.searchParams.set("limit", "50");

const res = await fetch(url, {
  headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_..." },
});
const { data } = await res.json();
// data.transactions: Transaction[]
// data.nextCursor: string | null
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Query parameters

All filters are optional, and a row must match every filter you send.

| Parameter | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `module` | `payments` \| `issuance` | Return one module. Omit it to get every module your credential can read. |
| `kind` | string | One `kind` from the module's list (see [Row fields](#row-fields)). Requires `module`. |
| `status` | `pending` \| `succeeded` \| `failed` \| `canceled` | Filters on the normalized `status`, not on `moduleStatus`. |
| `custodyWalletId` | string | Exact SDP Wallet ID (`cwlt_…`). Up to 128 characters. |
| `counterpartyId` | string | Exact counterparty ID. Up to 128 characters. |
| `token` | string | A mint address or a well-known symbol such as `USDC`. For a well-known token, rows stored under either its symbol or its mint match. Up to 128 characters. |
| `search` | string | Prefix match on `id`, `moduleId`, or `signature`. 3 to 200 characters. See [Search by ID or signature](#search-by-id-or-signature). |
| `createdAtFrom`, `createdAtTo` | ISO 8601 datetime | Inclusive bounds on `createdAt`. Write the time in UTC with a `Z` suffix (`2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`); offsets such as `+02:00` are rejected. |
| `cursor` | string | The `nextCursor` value from the previous page. |
| `limit` | integer | Rows per page. Default `50`, minimum `1`, maximum `100`. |

An invalid query returns `400` with `BAD_REQUEST`. Common causes: `kind` without `module`, a `kind` that belongs to a different module, a datetime with an offset, a `search` shorter than 3 characters, or a `limit` above 100.

### Response

```json title="Response"
{
  "data": {
    "transactions": [
      {
        "id": "xfr_abc123",
        "moduleId": "xfr_abc123",
        "module": "payments",
        "kind": "pay",
        "status": "succeeded",
        "moduleStatus": "finalized",
        "organizationId": "org_123",
        "projectId": "prj_123",
        "custodyWalletId": "cwlt_123",
        "custodyWalletLabel": "Treasury",
        "token": "9aBCd...4eEf",
        "amount": "100.00",
        "counterpartyId": null,
        "signature": "5Kd3...Qe7z",
        "createdAt": "2026-09-15T10:00:00.000Z"
      },
      {
        "id": "ttx_def456",
        "moduleId": "ttx_def456",
        "module": "issuance",
        "kind": "mint",
        "status": "pending",
        "moduleStatus": "processing",
        "organizationId": "org_123",
        "projectId": "prj_123",
        "custodyWalletId": "cwlt_456",
        "custodyWalletLabel": null,
        "token": "7fGhJ...2kLm",
        "amount": null,
        "counterpartyId": null,
        "signature": null,
        "createdAt": "2026-09-15T09:58:12.000Z"
      }
    ],
    "nextCursor": "eyJjcmVhdGVkQXQiOiIyMDI2LTA5LTE1VDA5OjU4OjEyLjAwMFoi..."
  },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "timestamp": "2026-09-15T10:00:05.000Z" }
}
```

`nextCursor` is `null` on the last page. The response has no total count.

## Row fields

### Fields on every row

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Row identifier. Use it as your key for the row. |
| `module` | string | The module the row belongs to: `payments` or `issuance`. |
| `moduleId` | string | ID of the underlying record. Pass it to the module's own endpoints. |
| `kind` | string | What the transaction did. The values depend on `module`. |
| `status` | `pending` \| `succeeded` \| `failed` \| `canceled` | Normalized status, with the same four values for every module. |
| `moduleStatus` | string | The underlying record's own status. The values depend on `module`. |
| `organizationId` | string | Your organization ID. |
| `projectId` | string \| null | The project the record belongs to. |
| `custodyWalletId` | string \| null | SDP Wallet ID on the record. |
| `custodyWalletLabel` | string \| null | That wallet's label. `null` when the wallet has no label or the row has no wallet. |
| `token` | string \| null | The token the row moved or acted on. The format depends on `module`. |
| `amount` | string \| null | Exact decimal string in token units: `"100.00"` is 100 tokens. `null` when there is no amount to show. |
| `counterpartyId` | string \| null | The counterparty tied to the record, if any. |
| `signature` | string \| null | Solana transaction signature, once there is one. |
| `createdAt` | string | ISO 8601 time the underlying record was created. The list is sorted on it. |

### Payments rows

| `kind` | Row |
| --- | --- |
| `pay` | An outbound transfer, for example from `POST /v1/payments/transfers`. |
| `batch_pay` | One Solana transaction of a [transfer batch](/docs/payments/send-payouts). |
| `recurring_pay` | A transfer that collected a recurring payment. |
| `deposit` | An inbound transfer. |
| `onramp` | An on-ramp transfer. |
| `offramp` | An off-ramp transfer. |
| `confidential_pay`, `request_deposit` | Produced by payment features that are not generally available. Accept these values instead of failing on them. |

`moduleStatus` holds the transfer status described in [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification#status-lifecycle). It maps to `status` like this:

| `moduleStatus` | `status` |
| --- | --- |
| `pending`, `processing`, `awaiting_payment`, `settling` | `pending` |
| `confirmed`, `finalized`, `completed` | `succeeded` |
| `failed` | `failed` |
| `canceled`, `expired` | `canceled` |

Check `moduleStatus` before you act on a payment:

- For a wallet transfer, `succeeded` covers `confirmed` as well as `finalized`. Wait for `finalized` before irreversible side effects, as [Finality on Solana](/docs/payments/accept-verification#finality-on-solana) recommends.
- An `onramp` or `offramp` row has finished only when `moduleStatus` is `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, or `expired`.

Other fields on payments rows:

- `token` holds the transfer's `token` value as stored, which is a symbol on some rows and a mint address on others. Filter with `token` to match both forms of a well-known token.
- On a `batch_pay` row, `amount` is the total paid in that one transaction, and `counterpartyId` is set only when the transaction paid a single recipient.

### Issuance rows

| `kind` | Operation | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deploy` | Token deployment | [Deploy a Token](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token) |
| `mint`, `burn`, `force_burn` | Supply changes | [Mint and Burn](/docs/tokens/mint-and-burn) |
| `freeze`, `unfreeze`, `seize`, `pause`, `unpause` | Compliance controls | [Freeze and Compliance](/docs/tokens/freeze-and-compliance) |
| `update_authority` | Authority change | [Manage Token Settings](/docs/tokens/manage-token-settings) |

`moduleStatus` holds the token transaction status:

| `moduleStatus` | `status` |
| --- | --- |
| `pending`, `processing` | `pending` |
| `confirmed`, `finalized` | `succeeded` |
| `failed` | `failed` |

Issuance rows are never `canceled`.

Other fields on issuance rows:

- `token` is the token's mint address, or `null` if the token has no mint address yet.
- `amount` and `counterpartyId` are always `null`. For operation details such as `params`, `slot`, `fee`, and `error`, find the record by its `moduleId` in `GET /v1/issuance/transactions`.
- `custodyWalletId` is the SDP wallet that signed the operation, when SDP recorded one. The `custodyWalletId` filter on this list matches that wallet only. On `GET /v1/issuance/transactions`, the same filter matches every transaction the wallet's address took part in.

## Pagination

Rows are sorted by `createdAt`, newest first. Rows with the same `createdAt` are ordered by `module` and then `id`, so the order is the same on every request.

1. Make the first request without `cursor`.
2. If `nextCursor` is not `null`, repeat the request with `cursor` set to that value.
3. Stop when `nextCursor` is `null`.

The cursor records where the last page ended. It does not record your filters, so send the same filters with every page. Rows created after your first request don't shift the pages that follow; they appear at the top of the list the next time you start from the first page. Treat the cursor as an opaque string. A cursor the API can't read returns `400` with `BAD_REQUEST`.

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/transactions?module=payments&limit=100&cursor=eyJjcmVhdGVkQXQiOiIyMDI2LTA5LTE1VDA5OjU4OjEyLjAwMFoi..." \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="list-transactions.ts"
async function* listTransactions(filters: Record<string, string>) {
  let cursor: string | null = null;
  while (true) {
    const url = new URL("https://api.solana.com/v1/transactions");
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(filters)) {
      url.searchParams.set(key, value);
    }
    url.searchParams.set("limit", "100");
    if (cursor) url.searchParams.set("cursor", cursor);

    const res = await fetch(url, {
      headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_..." },
    });
    if (res.status === 429) {
      // Over the metered quota: wait, then request the same page again.
      const seconds = Number(res.headers.get("Retry-After") ?? "1");
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, seconds * 1000));
      continue;
    }
    if (!res.ok) {
      const { error } = await res.json();
      throw new Error(`${res.status} ${error.code}: ${error.message}`);
    }

    const { data } = await res.json();
    yield* data.transactions;
    if (data.nextCursor === null) return;
    cursor = data.nextCursor;
  }
}
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Search by ID or signature

`search` matches the start of a row's `id`, `moduleId`, or `signature`, ignoring case. It is not a substring search: `search=xfr_3f9a` finds the transfer `xfr_3f9a…`, but `search=3f9a` does not, because the ID doesn't start with it.

- The term must be 3 to 200 characters long after surrounding whitespace is trimmed.
- `%` and `_` are matched as literal characters.
- A full ID returns that one row. Paste full IDs or signatures when you have them.
- `search` combines with the other filters.

## Permissions

Each module needs its own read permission:

| `module` | Permission |
| --- | --- |
| `payments` | `payments:read` |
| `issuance` | `tokens:read` |

- With `module` set, a credential without that module's permission gets `403` with `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS`.
- Without `module`, the list contains rows only from the modules your credential can read, and the others are left out without an error. If the credential can read none of the list's modules, the request returns `403` with `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS`.
- The `api_admin`, `api_developer`, and `api_readonly` [roles](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys#roles) all include both permissions.

If a key is limited to selected wallets through [wallet bindings](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication#authorization-layers), the list only returns rows for bound wallets whose binding includes the module's read permission. Rows without a `custodyWalletId` are left out. Setting `custodyWalletId` to a wallet outside the key's bindings returns `403` with `FORBIDDEN`.

## Rate limits

`GET /v1/transactions` has its own metered quota, which applies in addition to the [standard per-key rate limit](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication#errors).

| Scope | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Per credential: one API key, or one dashboard user | 60 requests per minute |
| Per organization: all keys and dashboard users, across every project | 240 requests per minute |

- Over either limit, the API returns `429` with `RATE_LIMITED` and a `Retry-After` header that gives the number of seconds to wait.
- If SDP can't check the quota, it refuses the request with `503` and `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` instead of serving it unmetered. Retry with backoff.
- Use `limit=100` for bulk reads. Walking 1,000 rows then takes 10 requests.

## Reconciliation

A polling worker that keeps a local copy of the list:

1. **Pull new rows.** On each tick, list with `createdAtFrom` set to the newest `createdAt` you have stored, minus a short overlap, and walk every page. Upsert each row by `id`. The overlap returns some rows you already have, and the upsert absorbs them.
2. **Refresh open rows.** A row's `status` changes after the row is created, but its `createdAt` stays the same, so a window that only moves forward misses those changes. If you have rows that are still `pending`, start the window at the oldest one's `createdAt` instead.
3. **Re-read long-running rows on their own.** If a row stays `pending` for a long time, such as a ramp transfer waiting for the payer, widening the window gets expensive. Read it with `GET /v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` using its `moduleId`, or with `GET /v1/transactions?search=<id>`, which returns that one row.
4. **Act on the right status.** Use `status` to group rows, and check `moduleStatus` before irreversible side effects (see [Payments rows](#payments-rows)).

<Tabs items={["TypeScript"]}>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="reconcile-transactions.ts"
const OVERLAP_MS = 5_000; // re-read the last 5s on each tick to catch boundary arrivals
const FIRST_RUN_LOOKBACK_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

async function reconcileTick(store: LedgerStore) {
  const newest = await store.newestCreatedAt(); // ISO string, or null on the first run
  const oldestPending = await store.oldestPendingCreatedAt(); // ISO string, or null
  const starts = [newest, oldestPending]
    .filter((value): value is string => value !== null)
    .map((value) => Date.parse(value));
  const startMs = starts.length > 0 ? Math.min(...starts) : Date.now() - FIRST_RUN_LOOKBACK_MS;
  const createdAtFrom = new Date(startMs - OVERLAP_MS).toISOString();

  // listTransactions is the paginator from the Pagination section.
  for await (const row of listTransactions({ createdAtFrom })) {
    if (row.module !== "payments" && row.module !== "issuance") continue;
    await store.upsert(row); // keyed by row.id; the latest status wins
  }
}
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Notes:

- Every 15 to 30 seconds is a reasonable tick for background reconciliation (see [Polling cadence](/docs/payments/accept-verification#polling-cadence)). With 60 requests per minute per key, a 15-second tick has about 15 requests to spend, shared with anything else that uses the same key.
- The `createdAt` bounds are inclusive, so a row exactly on the boundary comes back on the next tick too. The upsert by `id` handles it.

## Related

- [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing) — inbound transfers, including observed on-chain activity.
- [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification) — transfer statuses and finality.
- [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts) — transfer batches and the transactions they produce.
- [Mint and Burn](/docs/tokens/mint-and-burn) — issuance operations that appear as `issuance` rows.
- [Payments API reference](/docs/reference/api/payments) — full endpoint reference.
